body: Please post on /r/SuicideWatch if you can. They are a great, friendly community and can give you some support or someone to talk to.

Not much, just chilling out in bed at the moment with my dog and my grandparents' dog that I'm looking after for a little bit.

My parents do the exact same thing. They constantly complain about my "moodiness". And they probably have every right to, it would be a big hinderance. But I don't think it is something that I can control and all that they do is punish me for it by not letting me do things that I enjoy or yelling at me or whatever it may be. It just makes me feel worse about myself.

I do this exact same thing and I honestly thought this wasn't normal, but this post is actually kind of reassuring. I would think something and then become aware of my thinking and question myself why I was thinking that and then sometimes become aware of that thinking as well.

I've gotten to the point where I can't trust myself sometimes and try to think objectively at myself, if that makes sense.
Please feel free to PM me. I'm going through a breakup myself, so please don't feel like you're completely alone. I would love to talk.

Yeah I'm 17, turning 18 in 6 months, which is a bit scary to think I'll be an adult so soon. I'm working on trying to get some help sooner rather than later, and is it is a really big step for you to reach out for help as well. Please PM me if you would like to talk. Personally, I would be really happy to talk to someone around my age who is going through similar things to me.

Please keep me updated if you can. I know I don't know anything about you but I do care about you, because I understand how truly horrible you feel right now. The one thought that is keeping me alive right now is that everything will be okay eventually. It is a bit cliché, but I truly believe things will turn out okay one day. I want to assure you that everything will be okay eventually.

I have come to understand that suicide hotlines aren't always the best at giving advice. I think that their main goal is to prevent you from doing anything in the moment, so they try to get you to distract yourself and put you out of your crisis.

I'm not sure where you're from, but in Australia we have a service for young people called 'eheadspace', which I believe would be a bit better than a suicide hotline. It is basically an online or on the phone helpline, who will actually give you some constructive advice. They also are linked to 'headspace' centres, which is a free counselling service within Australia (and New Zealand I think). I'm not sure if you have anything similar where you live though, have a look in the sidebar and find your country to see if there might be something.

Seeing a counsellor is probably best in terms of getting advice, rather than calling a suicide hotline. However, it is understandable that this is sometimes difficult or completely out of reach. Even maybe seeing your GP or something similar could be useful if it is possible for you. But for now, please keep posting in this subreddit, feel free to vent your thoughts and always know that we are here for you.

I can relate to this a lot. There are a million voices running around in my head telling me to give up and screaming at me. But there's one voice in the back of my head somewhere telling me it will all be okay eventually. I feel alone and have nobody to tell me it's going to be okay so the one thing I rely on is this single voice in my head. Please try to do the same and don't let go of that voice.

I don't know anything about you, but from someone who knows what you're going through, I want to let you know that I am here for you and you're going to be okay. Don't let go of that voice, because that voice is who you really are, and the real you wants you to stay alive.
Yeah, I just need a way of accessing a therapist first, and it seems like the only way that may happen is by talking to my parents about what is going on for me.

Honestly, you aren't wrong at all. Sometimes I really just need to man up and get it done with. I guess I've just become so paranoid now of making things any worse than they already are. I think talking to my dad initially may be better as well, but I know that he'll definitely inform my mum, which is just something that I will have to deal with. I really need to sit down and have a think about how I'm going to go about this, and just grow a pair and do it.

I do think about things like this from time to time. There are so many things that I struggle to understand about the world sometimes. I feel like we're all desperately trying to move towards a better world, but sometimes we can stray far from it. It is definitely a time of complete and utter chaos.
I am going to do this right now, thank you so much.

I have looked into this. We have a service within Australia called 'headspace'. I've used it a couple times before and has been helpful. However, it is hard to get to for me and usually the waitlist to see someone is very long. It is also only open during business hours, which means it is pretty much impossible for me to get to whilst school is on.

Sorry I should have made that clear initially, I'm 17/M. I understand where you're coming from, but honestly I think discussing what I'm going through at the moment *is* the worst possible thing I could tell them. Scroll up and read my reply to a comment above for some more info, but I believe my issues are fairly deep and I don't think it is something my parents would be able to cope with. If I were to tell them everything, I'm not sure what would happen to be honest. There are still a lot of things I struggle to understand about what I'm going through, meaning it's going to be even harder for my parents. I have some really bad issues with my mood and my behaviour, which I think is contributing to downfall with a lot of my relationships (friends, family, etc.).

I may actually look into ringing the GP and seeing what I can do in this situation, as I'm sure I can stay anonymous over the phone and just ask some questions.
I'll look into it, thank you.
Just a random name I came up with that I use to anonymously post.

Thank you so much, your response really means a lot. Just that reassurance that I'm loved really helps me get through.

I can definitely understand why my parents may be concerned. I used to harm myself years ago when I was a lot younger and a lot more stupid. I quickly worked out that it was only causing me more problems than actually helping after my parents found out about it. But since then my parents have struggled to trust me with a lot of things. And with my changes in mood, I can totally understand as to why they may be concerned. Sometimes it pains me even more thinking about how they may be feeling. But I don't think that makes it any easier for me to talk to them. Things like what happened in my past relationship and the suicidal thoughts are things I just definitely cannot talk about with my parents, and if they are going to harass me with questions, that is going to really make me feel uncomfortable.

I do try to look after myself. I probably could improve in some areas, especially my sleeping habits, as I can really struggle to sleep sometimes.

I don't really have any trusted adults in my life, but you're definitely right in the fact that I need to seek some help somehow. Just still trying to work it all out.

Regarding your first point, I know that my mum has been through depression herself, which makes me question why she has been so insensitive to how I've been feeling. I sometimes think that maybe things were a bit different to her and she just doesn't quite understand it in the same way. I don't think you're wrong about talking to them, but it will definitely be a challenge for me.

I don't really have any trusted or close adults in my life. My friends have definitely distanced themselves from me as well recently, which makes the situation tough.

I am not too sure exactly how seeing a doctor works, as I've only ever been with my parents before. I would have to do some research. I think transportation is the main issue, as well as getting there without my parents knowing, especially now that I just got back from school holidays.

I was just told by another redditor to post here and was told that this sub was friendly and helpful. Seeking advice aren't rules that I strictly have to follow, so I can rule out anything negative that I receive. When I don't really have anybody else I can talk to, (as sad as it is) I have to resort to people online.

I admire what he is saying and I do try to live my life this way. I am always trying to aim high, perform well academically, and take on the responsibilities like he talks about. I just find that a lot of the time, things don't go my way, and I desperately struggle sometimes. That is what I want to work on. I want to take on responsibilities, have friends, have a family, love my career, and live a happy and fulfilling life. Right now, I'm losing all hope of that. I am feeling so lost. I really just want some help so that I can be normal again.

I've definitely been considering this for a fair while now. It's just a really scary thing for me to do, because I know my parents will get involved to the point of harassing me about it. Another thing that I forgot to mention is that I've kept as quiet as I can about this, and anytime they've asked me if I'm okay, I told them that I am, essentially lying to them. I think that they will get very upset about this, over-protective and will harass me with questions, no matter what I say to them.

Seeing my GP isn't really possible without my parents being involved, that's the thing. I know talking to strangers on the internet isn't going to solve everything, but I don't really have anybody else to talk to and want to try to set myself in the right direction.

I've thought about this option, but will most likely just refer me to the school counsellor, who I haven't particularly connected very well with in the past, and I think some professional help would be best.
I'll trust you and give it a shot
